headword: お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}め

definitions.gloss: bento heating service; warming up boxed meals
definitions.explanation: A service offered at convenience stores where staff will heat up your purchased bento or food items in a microwave.

examples.japanese: お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}め⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{無料|むりょう}→無料：01662_muryou⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧？
examples.english: Is bento warming free of charge?

examples.japanese: お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}め⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{結構|けっこう}→結構：10387_kekkou⟧です。
examples.english: I don't need the bento heated, thanks.

examples.japanese: ⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦レジ→レジ：00879_reji⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}め⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦お{願|ねが}いした→お願いする：05654_onegaisuru⟧。
examples.english: I asked the convenience store cashier to warm up my bento.

notes:
お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}め refers to the free microwave heating service at Japanese convenience stores. When buying a ⟦{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧ or similar prepared food, the cashier will typically ask if you want it heated.

COMMON EXCHANGE:
- ⟦{店員|てんいん}→店員：00897_tenin⟧: 「⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→お弁当：02864_obentou⟧、⟦{温|あたた}めます→温める：02096_atatameru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧？」(Shall I heat your bento?)
- To accept: 「お{願|ねが}いします」(Yes, please)
- To decline: 「⟦{結構|けっこう}→結構：10387_kekkou⟧です」(No, thank you) or 「⟦{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}→大丈夫：00772_daijoubu⟧です」(I'm fine)

CULTURAL NOTE:
This question is one of the first set phrases visitors to Japan encounter at convenience stores, along with 「⟦レジ{袋|ぶくろ}→レジ袋：09531_rejibukuro⟧はいります⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧」(Do you need a plastic bag?) and 「⟦ポイントカード→ポイントカード：09835_pointokaado⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧」(Do you have a point card?).

USAGE:
Some items have specific heating times printed on the packaging. The service is free and standard at all major convenience store chains.
